reviews.text: Love all the new things that got added since the demo, but every time I run out of cards, I can't continue the game. Very sad, this is the second time I got stuck. I'll play again after an update, having no cards wasn't an issue in the demo, it would just skip the phase for choosing one. Edit: turns out a bug I reported for the demo is still in the game. Sure all the new content is nice but feels like the dev doesn't care much about properly fixing things before increasing the scope of the game.

[h1] 《Type or Die》简评[/h1] [h3] 一匹马的复仇之路。嗯？一匹马？ [/h3] 《Type or Die》是一款画风极具特色的以打字对战作为最核心题材的肉鸽like游戏。在游戏之中，我们将作为一匹马，一匹战死骑士的战马，拿起剑与盾，代替主人前进，并立下替主人报仇的目标而展开战斗。游戏有着浓浓的卡通绘本的风格，以及有些怪诞离奇的怪物，整体的搭配反而显得有些有趣，融入了肉鸽打字的玩法还是很新颖的。 游戏其实也没有太大的篇幅来介绍这些七七八八的环节，但是整体上还是很好懂的。我第一眼被吸引而来其实是这个打字的玩法，从视频页面上看着还是挺有趣的。自己上手玩，发现挺不错，而且能通过各种事件，减少，或者是增加我们的字符长度。当然，没打完自然也是会有着一些惩罚的。 游戏的依靠我们来投掷骰子，我们将会移动骰子掷出来的相应步数。当然，如果中途有怪物就会强制迎战。战斗结束之后继续往前走完剩下的步数。在战斗之中，我们能显著的看到生命值、攻击力、金币以及护盾值连杀数等。并且在规定时间之内输出屏幕正中的字符即可造成伤害，反之亦然。 与此同时，我们也可以使用获得的卡片，可以增加我们的攻击力、护盾等等，同时也有一些卡牌会具有除了数值增加之外的特殊能力，当然这些都比较依赖我们获取了。在我们前进的路上，有时候也会遇到或者发现宝箱或者各种事件等等，这些一般会给我们带来一些助益。当然也会有负面的事件，比如我就选过增加战斗文本词数的，可以说折磨死我了，太烦了！一开始还好，后面真的敲不过来！ 总的来说，这算是一款比较不错的打字题材的肉鸽like游戏，整体玩起来的话，还算蛮不错的，个人感觉很有潜力。当然对于这种小独立游戏而言，平稳落地更为重要，目前的demo也是增加了一些新的内容，感兴趣的玩家可以试一试，整体其实还算不错的，适合休闲的时候来锻炼锻炼手指。Hhh [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

Decent concept but like others mentioned the game is shallow in itself. Has rouge-like elements, like choosing certain cards that have debuffs and buffs, and holding other cards for later in a run to maximise their effectiveness has SOME strategy to it, but ultimately trying to be strategic in a game where a lot of the other things just haven't been considered at all. One example; gaining gold is basically pointless. One of the main stats in the game is your gold, however when you visit a shop the price of items is always around the same price as your current gold, give or take a coin or two. I understand why, as you always HAVE to buy a card, but honestly that mechanic shouldn't exist. You can also only buy one item per shop. This is infuriating if you deicide to maximise your gold on a run. Other uses for gold appear to be re-rolling post boss cards, which is decent, and a card that turns your gold into health, also pretty decent, but ultimately gaining attack or defence and forgetting gold completely seems to be more beneficial. Forgetting a stat completely tells me the mechanics and strategy weren't thought through enough, which is disappointing in a strategy game where there isn't much gameplay apart from typing a few words.
Fun game, I recommend playing in hard mode if you are fast with your keyboard! I wish it was showing cards we are buying/looting.

《Type or Die》是一款非常规主角的中世纪画风打字冒险游戏。我们将扮演一位骑士——具体来说，是一匹位失去了主人的马儿骑士。在主人战死沙场后，马儿拿起了利剑、发誓要为主人复仇，让夺走主人性命的怪物血债血偿，为此不论什么代价都在所不惜……投掷骰子决定点数，邂逅或趁火打劫、或心怀善意的NPC，谨慎地打出书中的卡牌，敲击键盘化作凌厉的攻势——让一个个字母组成的魔法借我们之手横扫敌人！ 话说在前头，本作的汉化质量实在是不敢恭维。这边用文字还原一下游戏主页面的显示内容： 退出游戏 排行榜 开始游戏 收藏 设置 设置 也就是设置出现了两遍嘛，问题不大。这样想着，我点击了开始游戏，然后在把启动资金用来开了几张卡后，游戏还是没能开始，此时的我意识到不对，然后点击了设置想调到英文看看是怎么个事……结果游戏直接退了。 ……感情“设置”是退出键是吧！ 那开始真正的开始游戏键是哪个呢，屏幕前的噶人焖？聪明的你们一定猜到了答案——对啦，是『退出游戏』！ 好在游戏终究是开始了。说回到游戏本身，采用的是走格子遇敌战斗的老一套，如果手头有卡牌，我们就需要先打出卡牌才能行动。而这些卡牌有正面buff也有负面诅咒，比如“把金币变成血量”，我的理解是消耗金币增强血量上限，再不济也是回血，寻思着手头就一块钱，回滴血也行啊。然而在卡牌打出后，我的最大生命值变成了1。哈哈，实在是太有趣了。 在冒险途中，除了需要打字击败的怪物们，我们还能遇到仙女、巫婆、劫匪和小丑等npc。仙女会给予强大的正面buff，巫婆则给出三个诅咒让我们任选其一，第一次遇到时可以给她一拳不拿诅咒，但之后就没这么简单了。劫匪顾名思义，会抢劫我们手里的一张牌，算是变相删牌；而小丑则会在我们完成填字谜题后给予奖励。 总体而言，《Type or Die》现阶段还需要多加打磨。汉化暂且不提，不能设置难度来对打字速度进行调整的话，手残如我到第三张图就没法玩了。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

I liked the concept, it definitely has potential if it gets fleshed out more. I wouldn't recommend at full price, but if it's 80%+ off then worth picking up. The RNG really does make or break a run, and there's a few different places where that occurs: - Forced card usage - Post boss battles - Witch encounters There needs to be a lot more words than there currently is. It also sems like the shops where mistankenly set to consume 100% of your gold rather than set amounts based on card rarity which is disappointing when you've spent a heap of time hoarding gold during the run to use on the collections chest post run.

Fun game to zone out with/waste time with. Given cards give enough options for progress. The jester, witch, fairy and wizard are nice adds. Would like to see: -> shop where the cards are not the cost of nearly the amount of gold you have, refresh option in shop, or option to exit without having to buy a card -> save option when you leave game in between ->with the wizard combining cards: that they really do turn into rare special cards.

I tend to have a hard time enjoying games, especially recently, but this game has been a nice break from that aside from the few complaints I have. Type or Die is addictive and interesting, but the game deserves some more love and care from the dev. Any use of AI in this project is disappointing to me and I do wish I had noticed before purchasing the game, I found the demo the day the game was released and I enjoyed it too much to notice right away, I don't think I would have purchased the game if I had. At first I thought the mismatched art style was jarring but I'd rather stock art be used for assets than AI artwork, I hope the devs will hire artists in the future with the funding they get from purchases of the game. I do think that this game should've gone into a sort of early access stage rather than being released in the state it did, but the bugs that come from being recently released are more inconvenient than game breaking so they're easily ignored for me. (Edit and disclaimer: I only have about 1.5hrs of actual playtime in this game, I left it open on my PC as the game doesn't have a save game option.)

I really like the game, great concept. However, there is a bug when the game tells me to choose a card after rolling the dice when I don't have any. There is nothing else to do than close the game. Happened with two games with 200+ kills. Edit: Tried playing a little bit more, but I always end up with the bug I described earlier, so I am not going to play until this bug gets fixed. Other opinions - wizard doesn't really give you special cards. I give him two cards and get just a normal type of card. After giving him two cards, I'd expect some kind of boosted card. - i don't know how the randomness works in the game because in some games i never get any dice card, so I roll with one dice throughout the game and I am out of cards all the time. So the game is seemingly random but in a weird way - I would appreciate to see my active boosts because it's hard to keep track of everything you applied - I think the fairy and the witch shouldn't have 2 choices out of 3, that are the same (for example, I meet a witch and first option is "You only have one HP" but the second option is exactly the same). - The Market prices don't make sense, I always fear meeting a market because it's gonna take all my gold and it's just giving common cards. Not a fair trade. Hoping to see improvements on the game because, as I said before, I am a fan of the concept and I am hoping to play in the future <3
Great game! I recommend it !

[h3]Quasi-medieval manuscripts regurgitated through a LLM with a basic wordprocessing gameplay on the side...[/h3] Now and then you stumble upon a neat concept in the deluge of new titles on the steam, but sometimes they prove to be all smoke and mirrors. This time around we have a word game with roguelike elements and a quirky medieval manuscript artstyle that lured me in, only to lead me into an AI-riddled rabbithole with a developer who apparently wants to debate the use of AI, until they don't. The streisand effect is, well, in effect, and digging a bit deeper muddied the waters even more. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3756676378 First and foremost, the game in itself is extremely rudimentary. You roll dice, move a pawn (crimson steed!) across a tiled map without any form of clear function besides encountering monsters, chests, boons and banes. Each battle is basically this: a line of words that shows up, type it in time and deal X damage or take Y damage back. The various powerups in the shape of cards are added to this effect by giving damage, shields, first strike and other abilities. This part of the game was frankly quite a mess with unclear and inconsistent wording making most of the abilities hard to decipher. Sometimes gain HP means gain total HP, sometimes it does nothing, sometimes effects are permanent, other times they do nothing at all. This kind of guesswork got annoying fast, and the whole card-system could use a good quality control for consistency and actual agency.. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3756661589 [h3]Now to the skeleton in the closet... [/h3] The AI-disclosure on the steampage for Type or Die reads: [quote=Hunt Games on Type or Die released 25 Jun, 2026] “I want to clarify right away that I am not an AI enthusiast, though I understand that this topic can be sensitive for some. Type Or Die uses AI for card icons and sprite animations. All other aspects of the game (design, programming, voice acting, music, interface, and the majority of the artwork) were created manually. If the game achieves a certain level of success after its release, I will hire a specialist artist to handle all of that.” [/quote] This would be all fair and good, if not all the evidence would point elsewhere, and I would argue that quite a few of the sprites and code in this game has its origins in an abominable intelligence. A thing to add to the pot is that the previous title by the developer, Vampire Cat, clearly states that they don't know how to illustrate, and unless they have magically learned to illustrate in less than 7 months this is just more proof on the AI-pile. [quote=Hunt Games on Vampire Cat released 20 Nov, 2025] “To be honest, I don’t know how to model in 3D or illustrate in 2D, which is why I used AI as a support tool.” [/quote] All of this points to this being another developer that clearly understates the amount of generative “AI” used in their work, effectively torpedoing all the trust and goodwill I otherwise would have shown to a small independent dev. I asked the developer for a few snippets of the work in progress of the many characters and backgrounds, the music and the other assets that they claimed artistry over as a proof of concept to dispel this notion. He did however politely denied my request due to previous online harassment, so im left to make up my own mind as to if this is more than just lightly AI-assisted or not. And just to be absolutely clear, online harassment is frankly appalling, and if you do not appreciate a game, just refund, leave a review and go your merry way. Stooping to stalking developers over using AI is just terrible. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3756662126 However, this is not how building trust works. If you are a novice and underfunded dev, just admit to it, just use the tools available to you and clearly state what your intentions are, then I as a reviewer can take that into consideration while evaluating the game. Do not try to obfuscate the fact that you lean heavily into what probably is prompts and scraped artwork from other more illustrious artisans. Any competent individual will see through it, and it is clear just by glancing at most of the artwork and gameplay in this game that it is far from entirely human made. This very discussion will be more and more prevalent in this industry as well as others as the clutches of AI get more and more broad, and frankly it is not a guesswork I'm pleased to go through. I feel like we move forward into a time where quantity by prompt will far outshine quality by heart, and it is a sad thought indeed. [b]Conclusion:[/b] A buggy, inconsistent mess of AI-generated assets cobbled together into a rickety boardgamey construction that really could use some QA-work done. This one is not worth the asking price, and the developer needs to work on both their communication and transparency. What saddens me the most is that I REALLY liked the concept of this! From the art direction to the idea of a roguelike card driven word game, it all just turned out to be quite mediocre. I came here to write a review after experiencing a couple weird inconsistencies, and after reading other reviews I fear my comments are very much in line with much of the discourse about this game being AI-generated. First, let me say that I don't really follow game development very closely usually, so when this game popped up in my suggested games I just added it to my wishlist and bought it because it was a typing game and it had a medieval art style. However, as soon as I started playing the game I was confused by the lack of information about *how* the game was supposed to work. The way the cards you receive work is never explained, and instead you just have to learn intuitively how long each card might last, what it does, and whether or not it offers a permanent buff or a temporary change. While strange, I figured that since the game was kind of like a roguelike (if you squint) that maybe that was intentional, but it really doesn't make any sense. On a recent round of the Hard mode, I was offered a curse by the witch that said it would reduce my attack *by* 1. Instead, it reduced my attack *to* 1, which basically killed my run then and there. I have noticed more inconsistencies across the cards (sometimes I select and use a card and it does nothing or it doesn't do what it described it would but something else entirely) and zones (the full health zone never fills my health to a number that makes sense). I really want to like this game, but it is largely repetitive and if the majority of the assets are really AI-generated (I'm not expert in this area, but I do see the things other reviewers are pointing out) then I'm very disappointed that I ever spent money on this game. If you don't know how to do a part of game design, then teach yourself--isn't that the point of making something?
